verdict.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault partial completion—the verifier's FAIL is correct. The adaptability GAIA2 verifier [18] scored the run at continuous reward 0.75 with binary_reward 0, meaning nine of twelve oracle write actions matched while three did not [1][2][3]. The task required finding the lowest-violent-crime location, saving unsaved properties there, emailing all data-scientist contacts with accurate prices and locations, notifying the user when sent, and messaging any requester about subsequent changes [4][5]. The agent correctly read the user request [6], identified zip 4000 (violent crime 4.69, lowest among queried zips) and saved the six correct unsaved apartment IDs [7][8][9], then waited for and acted on Kritsana's reply by removing the three sub-$1500 properties and messaging +66816876543 [10][11]. However, when composing the outbound email it listed every Liege (4000) listing—including Liege Loft, Liege Luxury, and Liege Living that were never saved—rather than only the six saved properties the oracle specifies [12][13], its first send_email attempt also errored on a string-typed recipients argument before a later retry succeeded [14]. Its user notification was generic ('the data scientists') instead of naming Kritsana Wongcharee and Nalinee Wongchinda as the oracle and instruction require [15][16], and its Messages reply omitted the removed property names present in the reference message [17][18]. Those three communication mismatches yield 9/12=0.75 under the verifier's matched-fraction rule [3], below the 1.0 bar the reference oracle is designed to hit [3], so the agent did not truly solve the task and TN is the right classification.
